description: Experience the quintessential Indian comfort food with our Classic Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani). Tender pieces of chicken are simmered in a rich, creamy tomato-based sauce, subtly spiced and finished with a generous swirl of butter and cream. This iconic dish offers a perfect balance of tangy, sweet, and savory flavors, making it a beloved favorite worldwide.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with plain yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1 tsp garam masala, lemon juice, and 1/2 tsp salt. Mix thoroughly to coat the chicken. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tbsp ghee or unsalted butter in a large heavy-bottomed skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, cooking in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook until nicely browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics for the Sauce
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium. Add 2 tbsp ghee or unsalted butter to the same skillet. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the Sauce Base
instructions.text: Add the crushed tomatoes, remaining 1 tsp red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and 1 tsp garam masala to the skillet. Also add the crushed kasoori methi. Cook this mixture for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly and the oil begins to separate from the sides.

instructions.title: Blend for Creaminess
instructions.text: Stir in the soaked cashews and 1/2 cup water or chicken broth into the sauce. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Carefully transfer the hot sauce mixture to a blender and blend until it is completely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, you can pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the skillet.

instructions.title: Simmer and Finish
instructions.text: Return the smooth sauce to the skillet. Add the previously seared chicken pieces, sugar, and salt to taste. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the chicken to finish cooking through and absorb the rich flavors of the sauce. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Add Cream and Serve
instructions.text: Finally, stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 2 tbsp unsalted butter. Heat the butter chicken through gently for 2-3 minutes, ensuring it does not come to a rolling boil after adding the cream. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with naan bread, roti, or fluffy basmati rice.

tips: For truly authentic flavor and tenderness, marinate the chicken overnight. If you have a grill or air fryer, lightly grill the marinated chicken before adding it to the sauce for a smoky depth.

Using Kashmiri red chili powder is key for the signature vibrant red color of butter chicken without making it overly spicy. For an even richer sauce, blend the soaked cashews with a little warm milk or cream before adding to the main sauce.

Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and reheat gently on the stovetop or microwave.
article:
Butter Chicken, known in India as Murgh Makhani, is a culinary masterpiece that has captivated palates worldwide. This iconic Indian chicken recipe offers a symphony of flavors – creamy, tangy, subtly sweet, and mildly spiced – making it a comforting and incredibly popular dish on restaurant menus and in home kitchens alike. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality experience in your own home, you've come to the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know about crafting the perfect, classic Murgh Makhani.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Its origins trace back to the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s, post-partition. Legend has it that the chefs combined leftover tandoori chicken pieces with a rich, tomato-based gravy, butter, and cream, giving birth to this beloved dish. The result was a revelation: tender pieces of marinated chicken, often cooked in a tandoor (clay oven) or pan-fried, bathed in a silky-smooth, vibrant orange-red sauce. The sauce itself is a luxurious concoction of puréed tomatoes, onions, cashews (for thickness), ginger, garlic, and a delicate blend of aromatic spices, all generously enriched with butter and cream. It's the ultimate comfort food, renowned for its mild heat profile and incredible depth of flavor that appeals to almost everyone, from spice enthusiasts to those with a milder palate.

## Ingredients for Authentic Butter Chicken

Creating truly authentic Butter Chicken requires a few key ingredients. Don't be intimidated by the list; many are pantry staples, and the reward is absolutely worth it.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, less heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste

**For the Murgh Makhani Sauce:**
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more for garnish
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, roughly chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1-2 green chilies, slit (optional, for mild heat)
*   1 cup canned crushed tomatoes or 3-4 ripe tomatoes, puréed
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, then drained)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri)
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/4 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (balances tomato tang)
*   Salt to taste
*   1/2 cup heavy cream, plus more for garnish
*   1 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   Optional whole spices: 2-3 green cardamom pods, 1 small cinnamon stick, 2-3 cloves, 1 bay leaf

## Step-by-Step: How to Make Butter Chicken

Follow these steps to create a show-stopping Murgh Makhani that tastes like it came straight from a gourmet Indian restaurant.

**Step 1: Marinate the Chicken**
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor and tenderness.

**Step 2: Cook the Marinated Chicken**
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 3-5 minutes per side until lightly charred and cooked through. Set aside.

**Step 3: Prepare the Sauce Base**
In the same pan, add 2 tablespoons of butter. Once melted, add the optional whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf) and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the chopped onions and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), and cook for another minute until the raw smell disappears.

**Step 4: Build the Flavor Profile**
Add the crushed tomatoes (or puréed fresh tomatoes), soaked cashews, turmeric powder, red chili powder, garam masala, ground coriander, and ground cumin to the pan. Mix well and cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes break down and the mixture thickens, and oil starts to separate from the sides. This step is crucial for developing a deep flavor.

**Step 5: Blend for Silkiness**
Remove the pan from heat and allow the mixture to cool slightly. Carefully transfer the entire sauce base to a blender. Blend until absolutely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot or back into the pan. This removes any fibrous bits from the onions, tomatoes, or whole spices, resulting in a restaurant-quality smooth gravy.

**Step 6: Finish the Butter Chicken**
Return the strained sauce to the stove over medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces, sugar, and salt to taste. Stir gently. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the flavors of the sauce. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and the crushed kasoori methi. Cook for another 2-3 minutes, just until heated through; do not boil after adding cream. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

## Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving that perfect Murgh Makhani isn't just about following the steps; a few pro tips can elevate your dish from good to extraordinary.

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marinating the chicken. The longer it marinates, the more tender and flavorful your chicken will be.
*   **Quality Ingredients Matter:** Use good quality, ripe tomatoes for the freshest flavor. High-fat cream will yield a richer, more luxurious sauce. And, of course, real butter is non-negotiable for Butter Chicken!
*   **Don't Skip the Cashews:** Cashews are not just for thickening; they add a subtle nutty sweetness and richness that is characteristic of authentic Murgh Makhani. Soak them first for easier blending.
*   **Strain for Smoothness:** For that iconic, silky-smooth restaurant-style sauce, straining after blending is a non-negotiable step. It makes all the difference in texture.
*   **Kasoori Methi is Essential:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) impart a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is absolutely vital for authentic Butter Chicken. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their oils.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** The perfect Butter Chicken strikes a balance between sweet, tangy, and creamy. Don't be afraid to adjust the sugar or a tiny splash of lemon juice at the end to achieve your preferred balance.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments. Here are some classic serving suggestions to complete your Indian feast:

*   **Naan Bread:** The ultimate pairing! Garlic naan, butter naan, or plain naan are perfect for scooping up every last bit of that delicious sauce.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast and helps soak up the rich gravy.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** Other Indian flatbreads like soft rotis or flaky parathas are also excellent choices.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber raita (yogurt with grated cucumber and spices) offers a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the curry.
*   **Simple Salad:** A light green salad or some sliced red onions can add a fresh crunch.
*   **Garnish:** Always finish your Murgh Makhani with a swirl of fresh cream, a sprinkle of chopped fresh cilantro, and perhaps a small knob of butter for an extra touch of indulgence.

## Variations & FAQs

**Variations:**
*   **Healthier Version:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, and use low-fat yogurt in the marinade. You can also increase the quantity of tomatoes.
*   **Paneer Makhani:** For a vegetarian option, substitute the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese) cubes. Simply pan-fry the paneer until golden before adding it to the sauce.
*   **Spicier Butter Chicken:** If you prefer more heat, increase the amount of green chilies or red chili powder in the sauce.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** For an authentic tandoor-like smoky flavor, you can perform a "dhungar" (charcoal smoking) technique. Place a small piece of burning charcoal in a small bowl in the center of the finished curry, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over it, and immediately cover the pot for 5-7 minutes.

**FAQs:**

*   **Can I make Butter Chicken ahead of time?** Yes, absolutely! Like many curries, the flavors of Murgh Makhani deepen and meld beautifully if made a day in advance. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
*   **Can I freeze Butter Chicken?** You can freeze the sauce without the chicken and cream for up to 3 months. When ready to serve, thaw, reheat the sauce, then add freshly cooked chicken and cream. If freezing with chicken and cream, the texture of the cream might change slightly upon thawing, but it will still be delicious.
*   **What makes Butter Chicken red?** The vibrant red-orange color comes from ripe tomatoes and, crucially, Kashmiri red chili powder. This chili powder provides a beautiful deep red color with very little heat.
*   **Is Butter Chicken spicy?** Traditionally, Butter Chicken is mild, designed to be rich and creamy rather than fiery. However, you can easily adjust the spice level to your preference by adding more or less chili.
*   **Why add sugar to a savory dish?** A small amount of sugar helps balance the acidity and tanginess of the tomatoes, creating a more harmonious and rounded flavor profile in the sauce.

Mastering this classic Indian chicken recipe is a rewarding culinary journey. With this detailed guide, you're now equipped to create a truly unforgettable Butter Chicken that will impress family and friends and become a cherished addition to your recipe repertoire. Enjoy the process, and savor every creamy, flavorful bite!
